start.content: I am Mary, mother of James the younger and of Joses. I followed Jesus from Galilee and helped provide for Him there. At Golgotha I stood with Mary Magdalene and Salome. We kept our distance because the soldiers controlled the hill, but distance did not keep us from hearing or seeing what happened. Many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem were also there.

choices.text: What did you hear Jesus cry?
Who else can confirm your account?

forsaken_cry.content:
At the ninth hour His voice carried across the hill: “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” I knew enough Aramaic to hear the grief in it: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” Some nearby thought He was calling Elijah. That mistake matters—it confirms that the words were loud enough for the crowd to hear, even if they misunderstood them.
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: the_forsaken_cry

choices.text: Those are the opening words of Psalm 22.
And what happened when He died?

psalm_twenty_two.content:
Yes. He did not give a meaningless cry. He gave us the first line of a psalm about the righteous sufferer—mocked, surrounded, pierced, and finally vindicated before the nations. I had heard that psalm before. I never expected to hear it spoken from a Roman cross.
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: the_forsaken_cry

choices.text: Tell me about His final moment.

manner_of_death.content:
He gave another loud cry and breathed His last. His death did not look like a man merely fading into silence. The centurion stood facing Him and watched the manner of His death. When he saw it, he said, “Surely this man was the Son of God.” A Roman officer supplied that judgment; Salome and I witnessed the same moment from among the women.
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: manner_of_death_testimony

women_present.content:
Mary Magdalene was there. Salome was there. I was there. And many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem were also there. We had followed and served Him in Galilee. We watched the darkness, heard His cry, saw the way He died, and later watched where Joseph laid Him. The burial and the empty tomb did not begin with strangers trying to reconstruct the story—we followed the same body from the cross to the grave.
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: distant_witnesses

choices.text: You also watched the manner of His death.

corroborated.content:
Our accounts meet at the same facts. The women heard the Aramaic cry. The centurion saw how He died. Salome and I saw both. None of us occupied the same place or carried the same expectations, yet the testimony converges.
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: distant_witnesses
